sections.html:
Carlsbad is the county seat of Eddy County, in the southeast corner of New Mexico. According to Wikipedia, it straddles the Pecos River at the eastern edge of the Guadalupe Mountains, in the northern reaches of the Chihuahuan Desert, at an elevation of 3,295 feet.

U.S. Routes 62/180 and 285 meet at the center of town. Wikipedia gives these road distances from Carlsbad:

DestinationDistanceRoute
Artesia, NM36 miles northUS 285
Pecos, TX86 miles southUS 285
Hobbs, NM69 miles northeastUS 62/180
El Paso, TX169 miles southwestUS 62/180
Carlsbad Caverns National Park20 miles southwestPark road

The city covers 29.2 square miles, and the Pecos River passes east of downtown. Carlsbad is the principal city of the Carlsbad-Artesia micropolitan area, which Wikipedia puts at 62,314 people. The 2020 Census counted 32,238 in the city itself.

The settlement was christened Eddy on September 15, 1888, after Charles B. Eddy of the Eddy-Bissell Livestock Company, and was organized as a municipal corporation in 1893. The town later voted to change its name to Carlsbad, after the European spa Karlsbad in Bohemia, because of its mineral springs.

Irrigation shaped the layout. Avalon Dam was built upstream, canals carried water into town, and the Pecos River Flume was built where the canals met the river. Wikipedia reports the Pecos Valley Railroad arrived in 1891, cowboys re-discovered the caverns in 1901, and Carlsbad Caverns National Park was established on May 14, 1930. Carlsbad was proclaimed a city on March 25, 1918, once it passed 2,000 residents.

sections.h2: What does the Carlsbad economy depend on?
sections.html:
Mineral extraction, nuclear waste storage and tourism. Wikipedia says the city overlies oil and gas formations of the Permian Basin and produces more potash than any other location in the United States.

  • Potash: discovered near Carlsbad in 1925. Mosaic Potash Carlsbad and Intrepid Potash operate mines east of the city.
  • Oil and gas: Wikipedia describes a current boom, with families and individuals moving to Carlsbad as employment rose.
  • Waste Isolation Pilot Plant: the DOE's Carlsbad Field Office operates WIPP, which Congress authorized in 1979. The first waste shipment arrived in 1999.
  • Tourism: Carlsbad Caverns, Guadalupe Mountains National Park, the Living Desert Zoo and Gardens State Park and the Christmas on the Pecos light show are all within fifty miles.

Employment tied to energy goes up and down with the industry. That swing is why Carlsbad owners sometimes sell on short notice, either because a job ended or because a transfer came through. Wikipedia does not give a sale count, so we do not state one.

sections.h2: How does the Pecos River shape the city?
sections.html:
Most of the water inside city limits is the Pecos River and the Lake Carlsbad recreation area, which together make up 0.93 percent of the city's area. The river flows into the northern part of Carlsbad downstream from Lake Avalon and Brantley Lake, passes east of downtown, and leaves in the southeast.

That puts a recreation corridor through the middle of town, and for sellers it means two practical checks. Look at which side of the river the house is on when you plan a showing route, and confirm the flood zone for the parcel. A river-adjacent house is the sort of property where a buyer's lender may require flood insurance, though that depends on the FEMA map for the address and not on the city name.

sections.h2: What is the Carlsbad climate and what does it mean for a house?
sections.html:
Carlsbad has a hot semi-arid climate, with dry mild winters and very hot summers. Wikipedia reports an average of about 35 days a year above 100 degrees Fahrenheit, with the maximum rainfall in July. Its recorded extremes run from minus 16 degrees on January 11, 1962 to 114 degrees on June 28, 1994.

  • Cooling load is high, so an old air conditioner or evaporative cooler is a likely repair item.
  • Nights below freezing are common in winter, which matters for exposed plumbing in a vacant house.
  • A river city has its own concerns: if a house is close to the Pecos, check the flood zone on the FEMA map before you talk to buyers.

The FEMA Flood Map Service Center is the place to check a specific address.

sections.h2: When are Eddy County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Eddy County lists the first installment as due November 10 of the tax year and delinquent after December 10, and the second as due the following April 10 and delinquent after May 10. The Treasurer's page highlights December 10 as the last day to pay first-half taxes without penalty and interest, and May 10 for the second half.

  • The Eddy County Assessor values the property and can be reached at 575-885-3813, according to the county FAQ.
  • The Treasurer's office, at 575-885-3913, handles payment information, and the county offers online payment.
  • The City of Carlsbad does not send a separate property tax bill, because New Mexico counties bill and collect.

If you are selling a house with a balance due, ask the title company to request a current payoff. Delinquent tax, with its interest, is paid from your sale proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: What are Carlsbad's schools, college and airport?
sections.html:
Carlsbad Municipal Schools is the public school district. It operates Carlsbad High School, Carlsbad Early College High School and a charter school, Jefferson Montessori Academy, per Wikipedia. New Mexico State University has a branch campus in Carlsbad with about 2,000 students.

Cavern City Air Terminal sits just south of town. Wikipedia reports Contour Airlines offering non-stop service to Albuquerque and Denver, which a relocating owner may find useful for scheduling a closing from out of town.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house in Carlsbad?
sections.html:
The same three routes apply here as anywhere in New Mexico: list with an agent, sell by owner, or take a cash offer.

  • List with an agent: useful if the house is in good shape and you can wait out showings, inspection and a buyer's loan.
  • Sell by owner: avoids commission but puts marketing and legal paperwork on you.
  • Cash buyer: no lender, no repair negotiation, and a closing date that follows your timeline.

A cash offer is usually lower than a fully repaired retail sale, and we do not quote one before seeing the house. It tends to suit a house that needs cooling or roof work, an inherited property, a rental with a tenant, or a seller who is leaving the area soon. Closing runs through a title company, which pays off the mortgage, liens and any tax owed.

faqs.a: Carlsbad is the county seat of Eddy County in southeastern New Mexico, on the Pecos River at the eastern edge of the Guadalupe Mountains. Carlsbad Caverns National Park is about 20 miles southwest.

faqs.q: When are Eddy County property taxes due?
faqs.a: First-half tax is due November 10 and delinquent after December 10. Second-half tax is due April 10 and delinquent after May 10.

faqs.q: What are the main employers in the Carlsbad area?
faqs.a: Wikipedia names potash mining, oil and gas production in the Permian Basin, the DOE's Waste Isolation Pilot Plant and tourism, including Carlsbad Caverns National Park.

faqs.q: Does the oil and gas industry affect selling a house in Carlsbad?
faqs.a: It can. Wikipedia describes an oil and gas boom that drew workers to Carlsbad, so job changes in that industry can lead owners to sell quickly or move.
Wikipedia reports about 35 days a year above 100 degrees Fahrenheit, with a record high of 114 degrees. Cooling systems are a common inspection focus.

faqs.q: Who values and bills property tax in Carlsbad?
faqs.a: The Eddy County Assessor values it and the Eddy County Treasurer bills and collects. The city does not issue a separate bill.
